title: Scrambled Letters and Hash
description: Implement a string scrambler with six operation types, then reverse it to recover the original password.
writeup:
## Approach

This is a straightforward interpreter problem: implement each of the six scrambling operations, then apply them in sequence.

The trickiest operation is **rotate based on position**: find the current index of a letter, then rotate right by `1 + index + (1 if index ≥ 4 else 0)`. The extra rotation when the index is ≥ 4 is easy to miss.

## Part 1

Apply all operations to `"abcdefgh"` in order and return the result.

## Part 2

Find the input to `"fbgdceah"`. Rather than inverting each operation (the rotate-based rule is particularly awkward to reverse), the simpler approach is to try all permutations of the 8 characters. `8! = 40,320` — each permutation is scrambled and checked against the target. Python's `itertools.permutations` makes this concise and fast enough to run in well under a second.
